title: Flow-control horizon and tenant commitment reconciler
author: Priya Shah
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets see frequent short-lived microbursts from interactive tenants that current autoscaler windows either over-provision for or react to too late. This PR introduces a new autoscaler mode, "flow_control_horizon", that maintains a short rolling horizon of preallocated transient commitments for tenants and a Commitment Reconciler that continuously converts longer-term reserved capacity into shorter-term transient allocations when forecasts indicate imminent burst demand. The goal is to reduce 95/99th token latency during spikes while keeping steady-state commit costs stable. Changes include algorithm design, operator config knobs, telemetry, backward-compatible runtime flags, and an incremental rollout plan. Key points: 1) Horizon allocator: predictive short-window allocation using exponential-weighted burst forecasts and decay-backed headroom. 2) Commitment Reconciler: maps long-term reservations to horizon slots with safety checks and soft-grace windows to avoid churn. 3) Telemetry: new tenant-level percentiles and reconciliation event counters for SLO validation. 4) Safety: canary rollout, runtime flags to switch between existing allocation and flow_control_horizon, and automatic rollback when reconciliation_error_rate exceeds threshold. Linear references: ENG-5421 ENG-5489. Deployment plan: stage 1 enable telemetry-only for 24h; stage 2 enable horizon allocator in beta clusters with limited tenants; stage 3 global rollout with throttles. Rollback: flip feature flag and drain any horizon slots via reconciler dry-run. See docs/ops/flow-control-horizon.md for operator guidance.

release_notes: Introduces flow_control_horizon autoscaler mode and Commitment Reconciler to preallocate transient tenant capacity based on short-horizon burst forecasts. Adds tenant_commit_pct_p95 and tenant_commit_pct_p99, flow_horizon_headroom, and reconciliation_events_total metrics. Rollout via feature-flagged canary, telemetry-only first. Backwards compatible and reversible.
review_thread: Leah Kim: Can you explain the safety threshold behaviour if the reconciler oversubscribes? Concerned about double-allocating from reservations.

Priya Shah (author): The reconciler has a two-phase check: a dry-run reservation check against current live allocations and a soft-commit step that sets a reconciliation_lock per-tenant for 30s. If the error rate climbs we revert allocations under the flag. Added more unit tests to cover race windows.
Maxim Ivanov: Found a potential high-CPU hot loop in the reconciler core when many tenants have identical expiry windows. Suggest coalescing ticks.
ci_logs_summary: Initial CI run failed due to a flakey integration test (timing-sensitive); fixed by adding deterministic clock mocks and re-running. Final CI: all unit and integration suites passed. Performance benchmark microbench shows single-digit P95 token latency reduction in beta clusters.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: reconciler could transiently increase churn and allocation thrash under noisy forecasts. Mitigation: conservative default parameters, EWMA smoothing, reconciliation_lock, and staged rollout with telemetry-only first. Operators can revert via feature flag and the reconciler supports a drain mode to gracefully return transient slots.
testing: Includes unit tests for allocator math, reconciliation predicates, and two integration tests simulating multi-tenant microbursts. Benchmarks added to perf-lab harness with scripts to replay traffic patterns used in ENG-5421.
ops_notes: Operators should validate the new Grafana dashboard and watch reconciliation_events_total > 0 in canary. Default feature flag is off for main. See docs/ops/flow-control-horizon.md for step-by-step rollout and observable thresholds.
changelog_entry: Added flow_control_horizon autoscaler mode and Commitment Reconciler; new telemetry and operator docs. See release notes for rollout guidance.
